work: Countrey Contentments, or The English Huswife: household-order portions
heading: CHAP. IIII. Of Dairies, Butter, Cheese, and the necessarie things belonging to that Office.

items.text: Furnish the dairy with the best kine you can obtain: of big bone, fair shape, right breed, deep of milk, gentle and kind.
items.citation: Markham, The English Huswife, Chap. IIII
items.quote: Kine of the best choice and breed that our English houswife can possibly attain vnto, as of big bone, faire shape, right bred, and deep of milke, gentle, and kindely.

work: Countrey Contentments, or The English Huswife: household-order portions
heading: CHAP III. Of Wooll, Hempe, Flaxe and Cloth, and Dying of colours, of each seuerall substance, with all the knowledges belonging thereto.

items.text: Provide her with wool sufficient for the family's clothing.
items.quote: it is the office of the Husbandman at the sheering of his sheepe, to bestow vpon the Hous-wife such a competent proportion of wooll, as shall bee conuenient for the clothing of his family

items.text: Clothe the household outwardly and inwardly: with woolen cloth for warmth and comeliness, and linen for cleanliness.
items.quote: ought to cloath them outwardly & inwardly; outwardly for defence from the cold and comelinesse to the person; and inwardly, for cleanlinesse and neatnesse of the skinne

work: Countrey Contentments, or The English Huswife: household-order portions
heading: Chapter VII. Of the Office of the Brew-ho〈…〉ses, and the 〈…〉, and the necessarie things 〈…〉.

items.text: Provide wholesome and well-made drinks (beer, ale, etc.) for the household to preserve health.
items.quote: the English Hous-wife showes how to preserue health by wholsome Physick

work: Countrey Contentments, or The English Huswife: household-order portions
heading: CHAP. V. The Office of the Malster, and the seuerall secrets, and knowledges belonging to the making of Malte.

items.text: Be experienced and well practiced in the making of malt, for it is the work and care of the woman within doors.
items.quote: This office or place of knowledge belongeth particularly to the Hous-wife

items.text: Bring in and provide the grain, and excuse her from portage or too heavy burdens.
items.quote: the Man only ought to bring in, and prouide the graine, and excuse her from portage or too heauie burthens

items.text: Assist the housewife in all labors of making malt, from the fat to the kiln.
items.quote: the Art of making the Malt ... it is onely the worke of the Houswife and the Maid-seruants to her appertaining

work: Countrey Contentments, or The English Huswife: household-order portions
heading: CHAP. II. Of the outward and actiue knowledge of the Hous-wife; and of her skill in Cookerie; As Sallets of all sorts, with Flesh, Fish, Sauces, Pastrie, Banqueting-stuffe, and ordering of great feasts: Also Distillations, Perfumes, conceited Secrets, and preseruing Wine of all sorts.

items.text: Serve and keep your husband with the true duty expected, especially in cookery and household provision.
items.quote: she may loue and obey, but shee cannot serue and keepe him with that true dutie which is euer expected.

items.text: Order and set each dish in its due place at feasts, according to fashion and custom, so that the guests receive contentment.
items.quote: set euery one in his due place, giving precedency according to fashion and custome

work: Countrey Contentments, or The English Huswife: household-order portions
heading: CHAP. I. Of the inward vertues of the minde which ought to be in euery Hous-wife. And first of her generall knowledges both in Phisicke and Surgerie, with plaine approued medicynes for health of the House-hold, also the extraction of excellent Oyles fit for those purposes.

items.text: Give by her example an incitement and spur unto all her family to pursue the same steps of religion.
items.quote: giuing by her example, an incitement and spurre vnto all her family to pursue the same steppes

items.text: Learn from the worthy preacher and her husband those good examples which she shall see exercised among her servants.
items.quote: learning from the worthy Preacher & her husband, those good examples which shee shall with all carefull diligence see exercised amongst her seruants.

items.text: Desire less to direct than to be directed; appear pleasant, amiable and delightful; suppress contrary thoughts and call him home from error with mild sufferance rather than anger.
items.quote: coueting lesse to direct then to bee directed, appearing euer vnto him pleasant, amiable and delightfull... with a milde sufferance rather to call him home from his error, then with the strength of anger

items.text: Proportion her apparel and diet according to the competency of her husband's estate and calling, making her circle rather straight than large.
items.quote: she shall proportion according to the competency of her husbands estate & calling, making her circle raither straight then large

items.text: Prepare wholesome and cleanly diet at due hours, cooked with care and diligence, proceeding more from the provision of her own yard than the markets.
items.quote: let her dyet be wholesome and cleanly, prepared at due howers, and Cookt with care and diligence... let it proceed more from the prouision of her owne yarde, then the furniture of the markets
our English Hus-wife must bee of chast thought

items.text: Have a physical kind of knowledge to administer wholesome receipts or medicines for the good of their healths, to prevent sickness and cure it.
items.quote: it is meet that shee haue a phisicall kinde of knowledge, how to administer many wholsome receits or medicines for the good of their healthes

items.text: Together with her husband, be careful to bring up servants in the daily exercises of religion and bestow a small time morning and evening in prayers.
items.quote: the more carefull the master and mistris are to bring vp their seruants in the dayly exercises of Religion... a small time morning and euening bestowed in prayers
